# M0-d-08 — the first check's notes (minor findings, for the hardening milestone M4)

These notes come from the independent check of item M0-d-08, the time-dilation shim and the op-order /
slot-renumbering / issue-order harness (lane `check/M0-d-08`, flow flow-7, stage group 9, 2026-10-05). Under J180 none
of them fails the item; the verdict, its blockers and its evidence are in `checks/M0-d-08.md`, whose mutant ids
(C01 – C30, K01 – K11) and probe ids (P1 – P4) these notes use.

| # | finding | evidence | handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| N-1 | `renumberSlots` permutes the role-row slots (C-0199 (2); the renumber test's title says "role row"), but no test can fail when it does not: C21 (`rMap` the identity) survives. The item's own list is vertex, half-edge and face slots, so this is off the item's stated promise. | `C21 SURVIVED rc=0 Tests 36 passed (36) :: role rows not permuted`. | M4: assert that some live role row moves (as the test already does for vertices) and that each row's content lands at `maps.role[row]`. |
| N-2 | `recordPrint` sorts the demoted edges (`r.demoted.edges.map(...).sort()`), so the record's own demoted-edge order (C-0185 (17)) is not compared, although C-0199 (1) says the record's orders are compared. Kernel mutant K11 (demoted edges in slot order) survives; no fixture may demote two edges in one batch, so the sort may also hide nothing today. | `print.ts:320`; `K11 SURVIVED rc=0 Tests 36 passed (36)`. | M4: print the demoted edges in the record's order, and add a fixture that demotes two edges in one batch. |
| N-3 | Kernel slot-order mutants that the bars do not reach: K06 (the record's promoted / unflagged / moved vertex lists in slot order), K07 (a face region's pairs in slot order, `faces/common.ts:117`), K08 (mergeFaces' equal-length tie by face slot, `faces/merge.ts:134`), K10 (the record's role keys left in collection order). They need a batch with two or more such vertices, a merge between two equal-length candidates, or several role keys whose collection order differs from rule 7's; the constructive set's leading insertions do not build one. K07 and K10 may be equivalent (the pairs and keys may be re-sorted downstream, or collected in a slot-free order); PLAUSIBLE, not run further. | `K06/K07/K08/K10 SURVIVED rc=0 Tests 36 passed (36)`; K01 – K05 and K09 KILLED (see the check file). | M4 (or M0-k-04's runner): constructive fixtures with two promotions in one batch, an equal-length merge, a multi-role batch; then re-run K06 – K10. |
| N-4 | The constructive sequences take only a case's leading `insertChain` steps (C-0199 (3)); five cases insert again after another step, so their later insertions — among them the slot-reuse cases — never run under renumbering: `index/slot-reuse-stage`, `index/slot-reuse-districts`, `index/l3-order-after-l4`, `remove/tjunction-profiled-spine`, `limit/data-stale-slot`, `fix/tunnel-corridor`. The constructive arenas also never rebuild a static partition, so their indexes hold only grid items. | Probe P2 (census of `casesAt('M0')` at seeds 1 and 2): `LATER-INSERTS-DROPPED` for the six cases named. | M4: interpret `rebuildPartitions` and later `insertChain` / `removeEdges` steps, so the slot-reuse cases run whole. |
| N-5 | For `geom/cut-through-vertex` the harness's next op throws in the harness, not in the kernel: `constructive.ts` locates the face at the cut's middle point, which in this case is the face's vertex, so `faceHolding` throws and the outcome is `threw` plus the arena; the case's own expectation (a refusal, `E_NOT_TWO_CROSSINGS`) is never reached. | P2: `NONCOMMIT 1 geom/cut-through-vertex #1 next splitFace face by cut threw`. | M4: take an interior point off the cut (the case's `points` or a point beside the cut's first piece). |
| N-6 | "Every declared-form fixture of M0-a-07" is read as two batches the harness builds (C-0199 (3)); M0-a-07's one inline declared fixture (`kernel/test/faces/claim.test.ts`, "a declared batch of a split and a pin commits": `opPinVertices` + `opSplitFace`) and the ops `pinVertices`, `connectHole` and `absorbSliver` are not among them. The kernel passes them: probe P3 ran that fixture and a declared `connectHole` + `splitFace` batch through `permutationCompare` (16 orders) and `runTwiceCompare`. | P3: `PERM {"permutable":2,"orders":17,"identical":true,"div":null}`, `TWICE {"identical":true,"div":null}`. | M4: add the claim.test fixture and the three ops to `partitionerSequence`. |
| N-7 | The exit bar's words "op-order determinism … over the constructive set" are met by the callback issue order (`runTwiceCompare` on every constructive arena); the declared form is permuted only on M0-a-06's and M0-a-07's fixtures, which is how M0.md §1 (a) splits the bar ("the declared form at M0-a-06, the callback issue order and slot-renumbering identity at M0-d-08"). A declared-batch permutation over the constructive set's same-level chains would reach the coincident and overlapping degeneracies that attraction orders. | M0.md §1 (a) bar line; `support.ts` builds one callback batch per constructive chain. | M4: issue each constructive case's same-level chains also as one declared batch and permute it. |
| N-8 | `outcomePrint` prints a refusal by its code alone and no arena, so a refused last batch of a sequence never has its arena compared (a refusal must leave the arena at its version, §2.2 rule 8; an earlier refusal is seen through the next batch's arena). | `print.ts:334`. | M4: append the arena print to a refusal's outcome. |
